ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, partners, managers and controlling persons against the Luxembourg domestic sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, and international benchmark lists, including OFAC SDN list where USD-denominated operations are anticipated. Enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are mandatory for any person identified as a politically exposed person (PEP). Ongoing monitoring is required through the Luxembourg Business Registers/UBO register and CSSF guidance; any confirmed or unresolved sanctions match shall block the incorporation or the relevant transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (lbr.lu / rcs.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in a Latin-script member-state language; Luxembourg law does not require the name to be in French, German or Luxembourgish, but the name must comply with public policy, be distinguishable from existing corporate names, and not mislead the public. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. If the SCSp is to be commercially active within Luxembourg, the name must not give the impression of a governmental, public or regulated entity unless authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or appointed notary may submit a reasoned reconsideration request to the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR). If rejection is maintained, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Tribunal d'arrondissement du Luxembourg, commercial chamber, within one month of notification, pursuant to the rules governing the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Luxembourg Business Registers, as amended. The SCSp must retain legal counsel for the appeal and provide supplementary evidence of distinguishability and non-confusion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or administrative office is permissible for the registered office of an SCSp provided there is a physical address in Luxembourg for service of legal process. However, the actual stevedoring activity is physically carried out at marine docks outside Luxembourg, meaning the SCSp is treated as an investment holding entity and must not claim operational substance inconsistent with its Luxembourg administrative seat. Substance guidance requires at least one Luxembourg-resident manager or locally appointed corporate officer, local board or partner meeting minutes, and accessible accounting records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk: the CSSF, Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines, and the Luxembourg Business Registers may conduct targeted on-site inspections. The quantified probability of an unannounced physical inspection within any given year is estimated at 25-40%, rising if the SCSp is managed by a regulated fiduciary or maintains a bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 944-1 to 944-27 establishing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) as introduced by the law of 23 July 2016; law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; law of 11 January 2013 creating the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); Grand-Ducal regulation on the electronic filing and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), 14 rue Erasme, L-1468 Luxembourg; electronic filing via lbr.lu and MyGuichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration application Form C addressed to the RCS together with the fully executed partnership agreement (contrat de société), followed by the ex officio publication of the statutory extracts in the RESA electronic compendium.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital: the SCSp enjoys contractual freedom of capital and no escrow account is legally required. Partnership interests are subscribed and contributed according to the schedule in the partnership agreement; contributions must be made available to the partnership through a bank account opened with an EU/EEA or equivalent credit institution, and full liberation of subscribed interests is a condition for any distribution or repayment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions of the initial limited partners to the partnership interests, in the respective amounts set forth in the contribution schedule annexed to the partnership agreement, are hereby accepted, approved, and duly recorded. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the partnership agreement is ratified and the registered office of the partnership is established at [street address], Luxembourg, precisely as disclosed to the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] as general partner and [Name] as manager are appointed, jointly and severally, with full powers to operate, represent, and bind the partnership, to open banking accounts, to engage service providers, and to file all statutory registrations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution shall be effective immediately and all appropriate filings are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and bank domiciliation of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties acting under private signature (sous seing privé); notarial deed required only where contributions comprise real estate; account opened with a Luxembourg-authorized credit institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) stating the SCSp's name, corporate object covering stevedoring and loading/unloading of bulk cargo at river and maritime docks, registered office, duration, contribution schedule of the general partner (associé commandité) and the initial limited partners (associés commanditaires), profit-sharing ratios, and management clauses. Execute the agreement by all partners; open the SCSp's dedicated bank account in Luxembourg or in another EU jurisdiction, deposit the agreed contributions, and obtain the bank's anti-money-laundering KYC dossier confirming the beneficial owners and the source of funds. The notarial form is optional and may be used to facilitate third-party registration of contributed assets.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement with contribution schedule and profit-sharing clause
Passports and proof of residence of all partners and managers
Curriculum vitae and criminal record extracts of the manager(s) and the general partner
Bank KYC forms, source-of-funds declarations and bank reference letters
Certificate of good standing or equivalent for any corporate partner
Power of attorney where a filing agent is engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide audited financial statements or certified bank references of the ultimate beneficial owners; if a material term of the agreement is challenged by the general partner or a limited partner, execute an amending agreement before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS); electronic filing via lbr.lu with qualified electronic signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the standard registration application (Form C, declaration de constitution) together with the certified copy of the executed partnership agreement, the domiciliation consent or lease of the registered office, and the identity documents of the persons authorized to bind the partnership. Pay the official registration fee online and submit the dossier through the e-formation module with the qualified electronic signature of the legal representative. The RCS assigns the registration number and issues an extract of registration evidencing the legal existence of the SCSp for filings and contracting purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration Form C duly signed
Certified copy of the fully executed partnership agreement
Domiciliation agreement, lease or letter of consent for the registered office from the legal entity providing the address
Identity documents of the general partner and the manager(s)
Proof of online payment of the registration fee
Power of attorney to the filing agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond in writing within fifteen days, amend the partnership agreement where any clause conflicts with Luxembourg mandatory law or public order, and re-submit the corrected dossier through the e-form module without losing the original priority date where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of statutory extracts in the RESA electronic compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) – official electronic publication platform operated by the Luxembourg State, RCS acting as the transmitting registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the RCS automatically transmits the filed instruments and the statutory particulars to RESA for publication. The published legal notice contains the SCSp's name, legal form, registered office, corporate object, duration, identity of the general partner and manager(s), and the amount of subscribed contributions. Pursuant to the 1915 Companies Act, the partnership's acts and obligations become enforceable against third parties from the date of publication in RESA, subject to the mandatory rules on interactions with pre-publication acts.
required_dossiers: Statutory extract automatically generated from the RCS registration file
No separate filing is required; publication is effected ex officio by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published extract contains errors or omissions, file an application for rectification with the RCS and obtain a corrective re-publication in RESA within fifteen days; third parties may rely on the initial publication until the corrective notice is made public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Direction générale des PME, acting with the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce for commercial activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic application for the business permit under the amended law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsman, trader, industrialist and certain liberal professions. The activity of port stevedoring and bulk cargo handling is a regulated commercial activity requiring the permit. The application must evidence the professional qualification of the legal representative through a relevant diploma or not less than three years of professional experience in freight forwarding, port logistics or cargo operations, together with the absence of convictions and of personal bankruptcy. Upon approval, the permit is issued to the legal representative and must be displayed at the registered office and presented to the authorities upon request.
required_dossiers: Business establishment permit application form
Criminal record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire) of the legal representative
Diploma or certificate of professional qualification of the legal representative
Evidence of professional experience in port or freight activities
RCS registration certificate of the SCSp
Chamber of Commerce registration certificate
Lease or title to the operational premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusals must be formally motivated; the applicant may submit curing information to the Ministry of the Economy within a reasonable deadline and, in case of final refusal, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification or appoint a qualified manager and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the social security centre, tax administrations and the beneficial-owner register (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the business-creation formalities transmitted by the CCSS and register the SCSp as an employer, obtaining the employer registration number. File the initial corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) declaration with the ACD and obtain the business tax number. File the VAT registration form (Form 640) with the AEDT, electing the appropriate VAT treatment for port and stevedoring services; simultaneously lodge the RBE declaration through LBR identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than twenty-five percent of the partnership interests or exercises control of the SCSp. The general partner and manager(s) must also be registered with the CCSS as self-employed natural persons where applicable.
required_dossiers: CCSS employer registration form and list of initial employees
ACD corporate income tax and municipal business tax declaration
AEDT VAT registration form (Form 640) with activity codes
RBE beneficial-owner declaration
Bank confirmation of the IBAN and the contribution account
Copy of the RCS certificate of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where an administration requests additional information, respond within the prescribed deadline through MyGuichet.lu or by registered mail; if the RBE declaration is queried, correct the stated percentage interests and re-submit; statutory interest and penalties accrue only from the date of complete filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) for the business establishment permit; Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics) and the Administration de la navigation for the Port of Mertert concession and river-navigation operations; Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity for environmental authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (autorisation d'établissement) complemented by a Port Concession Agreement (convention de concession portuaire) with the Port of Mertert concessionaire and the Administration de la navigation, authorizing commercial stevedoring and bulk cargo handling operations within the port perimeter.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency) – Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity, 1 avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 (case-by-case evaluation) under the law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment: bulk stevedoring infrastructure on the Moselle river generally requires a prior integrated environmental authorization (autorisation environnementale) issued under the law of 15 June 2023. A full EIA report is mandatory where the project meets the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal implementing regulation of 15 May 2018, including port installations with a quay length of 500 meters or more, a works area of 10 hectares or more, or an annual cargo throughput of 10 million tonnes or more.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges into the Moselle must comply with the law of 19 December 2008 on water management and the applicable Grand-Ducal regulations on surface-water quality, including strict suspended-solids limits and a prohibition on oil-and-grease discharge; dust and particulate emissions from bulk handling must satisfy the emission limits transposing Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive), requiring covered conveyor galleries, water-spray dust suppression at transfer points, bag filters on silo vents, and continuous particulate monitoring; waste handling, storage and disposal must comply with the law of 21 March 2017 on waste and the circular-economy obligations, with manifest tracking for hazardous stevedoring residues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) following inspection of the terminal, storage silos, conveyors and office premises; structural load and stability certification for quay cranes, portal cranes, silos and conveyor gantries issued by an approved inspection bureau (organisme agréé) attesting compliance with Eurocodes and the Luxembourg building regulations; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including registration of all lifting and cargo-handling machinery, appointment of a safety and health coordinator for the site, validation of the emergency-response plan, and issuance of the workplace operation clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) following inspection of the terminal, storage silos, conveyors and office premises; structural load and stability certification for quay cranes, portal cranes, silos and conveyor gantries issued by an approved inspection bureau (organisme agréé) attesting compliance with Eurocodes and the Luxembourg building regulations; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including registration of all lifting and cargo-handling machinery, appointment of a safety and health coordinator for the site, validation of the emergency-response plan, and issuance of the workplace operation clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority) for VAT, registration duties, and indirect tax audits. Official portals: impotsdirects.public.lu, aedt.public.lu, guichet.lu, and lbr.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the SCSp partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through the eJustice/guichet.lu platform; RCS issuance of the 11-digit matricule (national business number) creates the base tax reference. Step 2: The AEDT links the matricule to the national identification number (NIN) used for direct tax filings; the fiscally transparent SCSp files annual information declarations only. Step 3: Submit the VAT registration application (form 645VA/TVA) to the AEDT; Luxembourg-resident entities apply directly while non-EU entities with a Luxembourg fixed establishment act through a Luxembourg fiscal representative; the AEDT issues a VAT identification number with the 'LU' prefix (LU plus 8 digits) within approximately 15 working days. Step 4: Register with the Customs and Excise Agency (Administration des douanes et accises) for the EORI number and, where applicable, an AEO authorization required for export declaration processing. Step 5: Obtain the statutory port terminal concession (Port de Mertert) and the stevedoring operating licence, both prerequisites for lawful taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is automatically fiscally transparent as a contractual partnership without legal personality; no national check-the-box election is required for pass-through treatment. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) an election to exercise a commercial activity, causing partnership profits to be treated as commercial income allocated and taxed at partner level; (ii) the ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch alignment under Art. 168ter LIR permitting symmetrical classification of the SCSp against a foreign partner's jurisdiction; (iii) the VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under the Luxembourg VAT Law to treat the SCSp and its Luxembourg taxable partners as a single taxable person; (iv) the limited-partner allocation rules which permit profit-allocation flexibility in the partnership agreement, subject to general anti-abuse principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979 and aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-enterprise exemption under Art. 57(1)(c) of the Luxembourg VAT Law (raised from EUR 25,000 as from 1 January 2023). The exemption is unavailable where the taxpayer is a port stevedoring terminal operating under a statutory concession, claims deductible input VAT, performs intra-Community acquisitions, or receives reverse-charge services; foreign stevedores with a Luxembourg fixed establishment must register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime is currently in force in Luxembourg. Invoices must comply with the VAT invoicing rules, be issued by the 15th day of the month following the supply, and be retained for 10 years. E-invoicing is mandatory for invoices addressed to Luxembourg public authorities via the PEPPOL network. Under the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) framework, Luxembourg will phase in mandatory structured e-invoicing and AEDT digital reporting for intra-EU supplies on a timetable beginning no earlier than 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: the 0% VAT rate applies to bulk cargo dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU where the terminal operator or exporter holds a validated customs export declaration and proof of physical exit from the EU customs territory. Services: stevedoring and cargo-handling services performed by the bulk terminal operator qualify for the credit-bearing exemption (zero rating) under the export provisions of the Luxembourg VAT Law implementing Art. 146(1)(e) of the VAT Directive only where the services are directly connected with goods being physically exported outside the EU or imported into the EU and placed under a suspensive customs procedure; written evidence of the non-EU destination, the customer's export status, and the direct link between the handling service and the outgoing international transport must be obtained at the time of supply. Intra-EU barge traffic on the Moselle and purely domestic stevedoring remain taxable at the 17% standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) validated and released by the competent Luxembourg/EU export customs office, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory

Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (sea waybill, CMR, or Moselle river waybill) evidencing carriage of the bulk cargo from the stevedoring terminal to a destination outside the European Union
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the export consideration in foreign currency within the 180-day repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency apply strict documentary scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. Where the export evidence bundle is missing, false, or untimely, the zero rate is retrospectively reversed and the stevedoring supply is re-taxed at 17% VAT; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month from the original due date, a 10% late-payment surcharge may be imposed, and administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 apply for intentional VAT evasion. Criminal VAT fraud is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years. The VAT assessment period is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or omission. Customs offences under the Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013) may additionally trigger penalty assessments and suspension or revocation of the terminal operator's concession and AEO/simplification authorisations; the stevedore and the exporter are jointly and severally liable for VAT on wrongly zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) – Eurosystem member; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, AML, and payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under the EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; no Luxembourg restrictions. Profit remittance from a transparent SCSp to non-resident partners is free of withholding tax and unrestricted; settlement via SEPA/TARGET2 or SWIFT is permissible without BCL approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timescale applies to export receipts in Luxembourg. Stevedoring revenue in EUR or foreign currency may be freely retained, hedged, or transferred abroad without BCL authorisation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility. Luxembourg-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions may support escrow and operational floats, but lack the direct SWIFT membership, correspondent network strength, and high-value clearing capacity required for the primary port stevedoring treasury. An EMI can be used for ancillary payroll, concession fees, or low-value port charges, but the main clearing rails remain with a tier-1 corporate bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the designated signatories and general-partner representatives is the default at top-tier Luxembourg banks. However, for a standard low-risk commercial activity such as bulk stevedoring, CSSF-compliant remote e-KYC via live video is generally accepted provided (i) notarised partnership deed, (ii) apostilled power of attorney, and (iii) certified UBO roster accompany an online interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed partnership principals or use of a Special Limited Partnership structure perceived as an offshore opacity vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RCS extract (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register), full executed partnership agreement, official beneficial ownership register (RBE) filing, and passport-grade identification plus proof of residence for every direct and indirect natural person partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and unexplained capital injection or subscription without audited trail for a capital-heavy port terminal build-up.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital call and subscription agreements, underlying investor bank references, audited investor financial statements, source-of-wealth report, and chain-of-funds documentation evidencing the lawful origin of each inbound transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure from maritime counterparties or bulk-cargo origin/destination jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Port concession or terminal-use contract, charter-party and cargo manifest, commercial invoices and bill of lading, BCL/CSSF sanctions-screening certificates, and a documented trade-compliance policy (including UN/EU/OFAC screening) applicable to all vessel calls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: SWIFT MT103/MT202 with reference to the SCSp's RCS number and BOP purpose code 'Direct Investment – Equity capital in an unlisted partnership' (BPM6/D.3). For EUR inbound, settlement is via TARGET2 using the receiving bank's central bank account; foreign-currency injections settle over correspondent SWIFT network. No prior BCL foreign-exchange approval is required; the bank performs standard KYC and transaction monitoring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cost-of-cargo and port service disbursements, settled on TARGET2 for EUR; (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) for bulk cargo sale settlements, payable at sight or deferred; (iii) port authority clearing via RCC/terminal management systems for stevedoring levies; (iv) MT202 COV for cover payments when a separate cover instruction is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX contracts (maturities standard up to 24 months in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
FX swaps (rollover of EUR working capital into trade settlement currencies)
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (for long-term USD-denominated terminal finance or BOT concession debt)
Zero-premium FX option collars (capped-rate protection for volatile bulk-commodity currencies)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for restricted currencies (e.g., offshore CNY) where a deliverable forward is unavailable; standard EUR/currency NDFs are generally not necessary.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (Annual Accounts Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the closing date of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory deadline gives rise to formal notices from the RCS or the Public Prosecutor; late filers risk criminal fines up to EUR 5,000 and, for persistent default, judicial proceedings that may lead to strike-off (radiature) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Annual Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), maintained by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the entity's RCS registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update beneficial ownership data is a criminal offence exposing responsible officers and partners to fines of EUR 125 to EUR 5,000 and, in serious cases, imprisonment; the RCS may also initiate ex officio compliance proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration fiscale de la SCSp (Annual Tax Return for the Transparent SCSp and its Partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the year following the tax period; the formal filing date is set by the Luxembourg tax administration and is typically included in the annual tax demand notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission triggers default interest and penalties of 0.1% to 0.25% per month on the assessed tax, with a minimum fine of EUR 20; continued non-compliance may lead to ex officio assessment, enforced recovery, and criminal prosecution of responsible partners or managers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises is mandatory for a SCSp if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average staff count 50. A statutory audit may also be required by the partnership agreement or if requested by partners holding a qualifying interest.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2008, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for consolidated financial statements and, on a voluntary basis, for separate financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SCSp must keep an accurate Register of Partners and must file any change in beneficial ownership with the RBE within one month of the transfer or event. Once a year, within one month after the RCS anniversary, the SCSp must confirm that the RBE data remains complete and accurate; failure to do so invalidates the good-standing status of the partnership and attracts criminal sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and General Managers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Luxembourg City aggregate headline rate for corporate taxpayers: 24.94% (17.00% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19% + 6.75% municipal business tax). An SCSp is fiscally transparent: no entity-level CIT or municipal business tax is levied on the partnership; partners are taxed on their allocated shares of the bulk port stevedoring profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp pass-through eliminates entity-level corporate taxation. A CIT-taxable corporate partner may benefit from the participation exemption (95% or 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains subject to ≥10% shareholding, ≥12-month holding period, and the taxable-substrate test). The IP Box regime (80% exemption; ~5.25% effective rate) is available only to CIT-taxable corporate partners. No sectoral CIT holiday exists for stevedoring; ordinary deductions, investment tax credits and accelerated depreciation under LIR arts. 102bis et seq. remain available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 560 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu – sociétés de personnes), filed electronically through the ACD e-filing portal (Guichet.lu / MyTax). The SCSp files one annual transparency declaration; each partner files its own CIT and municipal business tax returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December Y, the Form 560 declaration is due by 31 December Y+1; the ACD may grant an extension on reasoned request. Municipal business tax assessment follows the same declaration cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, Luxembourg RCS number, tax matricule, registered office, ISIC 5224 business code, and the statutory port terminal operating licence reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each non-resident partner with full legal name, foreign tax identification number and country of tax residence; a Luxembourg tax representative may be required to sign and file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 2 – Fiscal Year and Net Result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period and the net profit or loss of the bulk cargo stevedoring activity computed under LIR principles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The transparent result must be allocated pro rata to partners; non-resident partners are taxable only on the Luxembourg-source share of terminal income as adjusted by the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Per-partner allocation of distributable income: share percentage, allocated profit or loss, CIT-attributable basis, and municipal business tax apportionment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate or institutional partners must attach a valid tax residence certificate and retain beneficial ownership evidence; allocations to treaty-protected partners must be reconciled with DTA limitation-on-benefits and substance clauses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 4 – Loss Carryforward and Deductions Annex
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of prior-year loss offsets, deductible operating expenses, tax credits, and any controlled transactions with related parties requiring transfer pricing disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claiming deductions or treaty relief must keep contemporaneous substantiation (terminal service contracts, Port Authority invoices, crane utilisation logs, payroll records) available for ACD on-demand review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, partner allocation certificates, operating licence copies, and electronic signature of the SCSp manager (gérant) or appointed Luxembourg agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where all partners are non-resident, a Luxembourg tax representative must be appointed for service of process; all attachments must be digitised and submitted through the ACD e-filing portal.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office), an administrative fine of up to €15,000, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on the underpaid tax; wilful non-filing or false filing constitutes criminal tax fraud punishable by a fine of up to €125,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on dividend distributions; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% shareholding and ≥12-month holding period); DTA treaties typically provide 0%, 5% or 15% rates depending on shareholding and beneficiary status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief or the EU 0% rate: (1) obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the partner's home tax authority; (2) execute the Luxembourg residence/beneficial-ownership attestation (Form 22 model) confirming entitlement on the payment date; (3) apply to the ACD for refund if WHT was withheld at the statutory rate; and (4) keep holding-period, economic substance and arm's length documentation to survive anti-abuse review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law does not impose withholding tax on most outbound interest or royalties paid to non-residents (0%); treaty positions commonly apply 0–10% on interest and 0–5% on royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and ATAD anti-abuse tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File applies where the aggregate value of controlled intra-group transactions exceeds €1,000,000 per fiscal year; Master File and CbC reporting are required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least €750,000,000 (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 December 2019; ACD Circular LIR n° 164/2).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations code; however, substance is enforced through art. 6 LIR abuse-of-law doctrine, ATAD GAAR, CFC and anti-hybrid rules, the participation-exemption taxable-substrate test, and ACD administrative substance guidelines. An SCSp carrying on bulk port stevedoring must demonstrate real personnel, terminal premises, equipment, operational decision-making and commercial risk in Luxembourg to retain pass-through treatment and access to treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring stevedoring tariffs, demurrage and port-handling revenues at the Luxembourg bulk terminal; inflating deductible costs with fictitious invoices; or misallocating terminal profits to a non-resident partner to erode the Luxembourg tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of evaded tax plus monthly late interest at 0.6%; administrative penalty of up to 50% of the evaded tax; criminal tax fraud conviction carries a fine of up to €125,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years (LIR arts. 226 et seq.).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp gérant who sign false returns or knowingly conceal income are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; civil restitution (comblement du passif) in insolvency, asset freezes, travel bans during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment apply for personal culpability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox vehicle: no Luxembourg office, no terminal employees, no ownership of stevedoring equipment, no substantive management, with terminal revenues channelled exclusively to a treaty-resident partner lacking real economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD invalidation under art. 6 LIR and ATAD: revocation of fiscal transparency or denial of treaty benefits; income re-attributed to the Luxembourg stevedoring activity; retroactive reassessment with statutory interest and applicable administrative surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced against the general partner and directors where the structure was used to conceal the true beneficiary; criminal exposure under fraud statutes, director disqualification, and secondary liability for the tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Missing TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany stevedoring tariffs, crane or demurrage fees, or back-to-back Port Authority charges materially outside the arm's length range; failing to prepare the Local File within the prescribed period after ACD request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD transfer pricing adjustment to an arm's length margin; disallowance of excess deductions; documentation penalties and daily late-filing interest at 0.6% per month; aggravated cases may attract criminal tax sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving intra-group pricing without benchmark documentation expose themselves to veil-piercing where the adjustment renders the entity insolvent; co-liability for resulting tax, interest and social security debts may be asserted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the SCSp's beneficial owner declaration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within one month of incorporation or material change, or concealing controlling partners behind unreported nominee arrangements contrary to the Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to €250,000 per violation; publication of sanctions; potential manager disqualification; aggravated concealment triggers criminal money-laundering sanctions including imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and directors are personally answerable for RBE filing obligations; aggravated concealment leads to criminal prosecution, personal fines, travel restrictions and imprisonment.
